metas.name: Akkol Lamp Post Paint
metas.note: Akkol commonly uses a lamp post paint scheme consisting of a short blue stripe, a long yellow stripe, followed by another short blue stripe, and then yellow extending down to the bottom (image 1).

metas.name: Aktau Pole-Mounted Street Signs
metas.note:
Street signs in Aktau feature black text on a white background, enclosed in a golden metal frame (image 1). A circle at the top indicates the city district you’re in, and the pointed end directs you toward other districts.

Note: Many districts are labeled on the map, so you can use the information from the sign to find the exact location.
metas.footer:
Source: Street signs of Kazakhstan - by @kotyu.

Description and images - by @Docia.

metas.name: Aktobe Lamp Post Paint
metas.note:
In Aktobe, on some major streets, you can spot lamp posts painted light blue with a yellow stripe at the top (image 1).

I've marked all the streets where I've found them so far (image 2), though there may be more.

metas.name: Astana Surface-Mounted Street Signs
metas.note:
In Astana, you can find these street signs attached to fences or buildings (image 1). The design is fairly generic, but consistently used across the city.

Note: Spotting a different street sign doesn't rule out Astana.

metas.name: Atbasar Pole Paint
metas.note:
In Atbasar, you can occasionally spot poles painted in a burgundy color with a black stripe at the top (image 1).

Note: This paint scheme is used for poles holding street lamps. Poles without mounted lamps are likely either unpainted or use the Akmola color scheme.

metas.name: Atyrau / Semey Buses
metas.note:
In Atyrau and Semey, you can occasionally spot these light green buses with a white lower section (image 1).

You can distinguish the two cities by the coverage season and car meta:

  • Atyrau was covered in summer, while Semey was covered in autumn.
  • Look for a wire in the top-left part of the truck bed: it is present in Atyrau but absent in Semey (image 2).

Note: The wire may look slightly different or might not be visible due to the car blur.
metas.footer:
Source: https://www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

Description and images - by @Docia. Some information has been updated or expanded.

metas.name: Atyrau Buses
metas.note:
In Atyrau, you can commonly spot these eco-friendly, gas-powered Yutong buses painted in a light green and white color scheme (image 1).

These buses are also used in other cities across Kazakhstan, but if you can see the side of the bus, you may be able to distinguish it by the Atyrau logo, which is quite recognizable, even from a distance.

Note: Sometimes the bus may be dirty, making the logo less visible.

metas.name: Atyrau Lamp Post Paint
metas.note:
In Atyrau, you can spot lamp posts painted dark green at the base (image 1). Sometimes, there's also a yellow stripe above the green section. These are quite common in the suburbs but they usually don’t appear in the city center.

Note: There’s a good chance that lamp posts in other cities may also be painted in similar colors, so use this clue cautiously.

metas.name: Baltic Pine Forests
metas.note:
The roads north of Shchuchinsk around the lakes (image 1), are very distinctive — they are surrounded by Baltic pine forests in hilly terrain (image 2). Sometimes, you’ll even be able to spot lakes behind the trees. The coverage was taken in early August, so the trees are green and the weather is very sunny.

Note: Baltic pines can also be found in other parts of Kazakhstan.
metas.footer:
Source: A Learnable Kazakhstan - by @Capi.

Description and images - by @Docia.

metas.name: Car Dirty Vertically on the Left – Urban
metas.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car Dirty Vertically on the Left (image 1), you must be in the western suburbs of Ridder.

Note 1: The car is occasionally blurred, but the vertical dirt on the top left is still visible.

Note 2: A similar dirt pattern can be seen on a car in Semey, but that one does not have a bracket, which makes it easy to distinguish.

metas.name: Car with 1 Dot in the Middle
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 1 Dot in the Middle (image 2):

  1. A1, starting at Kellerovka, driving south to Kokshetau.
  2. A-13, starting at Kokshetau, driving east, then turning south at the intersection near the airport, and continuing up to the intersection with A1.
  3. An unlabeled road, starting at the intersection with A1 and driving east through Akylbay, along with some nearby offroads.

You can distinguish these roads by their driving direction and the surrounding landscape:

  1. Driving more or less south.
  2. Driving east or southeast. You can differentiate the southeast section (which has a similar angle to A1) by the gravel around the road. At A1 it's grey, while on the road near Kokshetau airport it's brown (image 3).
  3. Driving east. From almost every point on the road, you'll be able to see the village and the lake at the foot of a small mountain.

Fun fact: The Partially Blurred 3-Part Car driving on the A1 from Petropavl to Kellerovka also has this dot, but it's not visible. Google blurred the cars completely randomly some time after the coverage was released.

metas.name: Car with 1 Dot on the Left and a Dirty Back
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 1 Dot on the Left and a Dirty Back (image 2):

  1. A17, starting in the suburbs of Pavlodar and driving southwest up to the intersection near Turgay. A stretch between the intersection northwest of the Сасық көл lake and the intersection with P4 is covered by a different car.
  2. R-174, starting near Karaterek village, driving northwest up to the suburbs of Aksu.

You can distinguish these two sections by the number of roadways:

  1. Divided highway — the farther east you are, the lower the sun is.
  2. Single roadway — the beginning of this coverage is tricky: there’s no visible dot on the left side of the car, but the dirty back part of the roof matches.

Note: On A17, the coverage in the opposite direction was captured with a different car.
metas.footer:
Source: A Learnable Kazakhstan - by @Capi.

Description and images - by @Docia.

metas.name: Car with 1 Dot on the Right
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 1 Dot on the Right (image 2):

  1. A-2, starting at the intersection with Kb-23, driving east, then turning onto the road north of A-2 through Samsi, returning to A-2, and continuing up to Vodokhranilishche Shor-Koo lake.
  2. A-2, starting at Taraz and driving east, briefly leaving the divided highway to go through Shakbak Baba, and continuing up to Shymkent.

You can distinguish these two sections by landscape and weather:

  1. Up to Kenen, the sky is filled with dark, rainy clouds. On the short stretch of A-2 west of Targap, there is only one roadway. East of Kenen, the landscape becomes flatter, with no sizable hills.
  2. In this section, large hills are visible to the south. The weather is sunny — unlike the A-2 segment near Almaty. Between Taraz and Aisha Bibi, and near Shymkent, there isn’t a single cloud in the sky.

Note: In Shakbak Baba, the lamp posts are painted similar to poles in Taraz, with red, yellow and black stripes.

Note 2: You can also find this car in northeastern Shymkent, southern Taraz, and occasionally in Almaty.
metas.footer:
Source: A Learnable Kazakhstan - by @Capi.

Description and images - by @Docia.

metas.name: Car with 2 Dots on the Left and 1 on the Right
metas.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 2 Dots on the Left and 1 on the Right (image 2):

  • M-36, starting at a couple of kilometers north of Kurty, driving southeast up to the intersection with P-19, turning southwest and continuing up to the south suburbs of Shamalgan.

Coverage was captured during sunset — the farther south you go, the darker it gets. This section also has a distinct late autumn vibe, and, unlike the northern parts of the route, has no parallel road under construction, except for a very short section north of Kurty.

Note 1: If you see this car in an urban environment, you're passing through Shamalgan.

Note 2: The car appears blurred near Lake Sorbulaq.

metas.name: Car with 2 Lines on the Left – Non-Urban
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 2 Lines on the Left (image 2):

  1. E38, between Shymkent and Turkistan, with the car leaving the road only to bypass Temirlanovka. The road is covered in both directions.
  2. A-2, starting at the exit to Kumaryk, driving east, then taking an exit and continuing along the road south of A-2. At the intersection with R-39, the car turns north and returns to A-2, continuing its journey east. It then exits again at the intersection with M39 and drives further east up to the Kyrgyzstan border.
  3. A-2, starting at the intersection near Kenen, driving south up to Alga (where the car gets blurred), passing through Korday, and continuing via Өтеген көшесі to the intersection with Ob"Yezdnaya Doroga, where the car becomes visible again and proceeds east to the Kara-Su suburbs.

You can distinguish these three sections by driving direction and the sun:

  1. Driving southeast or northeast on a divided highway. The smudge on the left side extends into the middle of the roof (top part of image 2).
  2. Mostly driving east with the sun high in the sky. The smudge on the left is shorter and does not extend into the middle like on E38 (bottom part of image 2). If the car is not on A-2, it often passes through villages where you can spot various differently painted poles.
  3. Driving south, then briefly east. There’s no extended smudge (bottom part of image 2). The A2 section between Kenen and Korday has a distinct grainy, “salt and pepper” texture (image 3). The car is blurred in the middle of this section, but the road is still easy to recognize — grassy fields with rows of trees planted along the road, “Turkish” pavement, and the distinctive sunset coverage.

Note: The same car also covered some roads in Shymkent, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account.
metas.footer:
Source: A Learnable Kazakhstan - by @Capi.

Description and images - by @Docia. Some information has been updated or expanded.

Many thanks to @Top 20 of Ukraine for providing additional information!

metas.name: Car with 2 Small Dots on the Left
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 2 Small Dots on the Left (image 2):

  1. P34, starting at the intersection with A17 and driving south to Karazhal.
  2. A17, starting at the intersection with P34 and driving east up to the roundabout in Atasu.
  3. Unlabeled road, starting at Doskey, driving east, then north up to Botakara, passing through the town, then continuing east via Karagana-Karkaralinsk road up to Karkaraly.

You can distinguish these roads by driving direction, landscape, and time of day:

  1. Driving southeast through flat desert. It’s very sunny, and the dots on the car are hard to spot.
  2. Driving east at sunset. The farther east you go, the lower the sun is.
  3. Up to Botakara, the car is driving east and north. The sun is high in the sky, unlike on A17. From Botakara the car heads southeast, but the terrain features rolling hills, unlike the flat landscape of P34.

metas.name: Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted Antenna, a 'Leaf' Smudge, and a Dirty Back - Non-Urban
metas.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted Antenna, a 'Leaf' Smudge, and a Dirty Back (image 2):

  • M38, starting at Semey and driving southeast up to Qalbatau.

Note 1: The same car also appears on the A3 between Qalbatau and Oskemen, but it is driving northeast, and the sun is noticeably lower compared to M38.

Note 2: The antenna is not always visible.

metas.name: Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted antenna, a Dirty Back, and a Bird Poop
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with 4 Stripes, a Tilted antenna, a Dirty Back, and a Bird Poop (image 2):

  1. P27, starting at Korneevka and driving southwest to Botakara, then turning onto Karaganda–Karkaralinsk road and continuing up to the intersection with A17.
  2. A short stretch of P27 south of Bayanaul, driving west. The town of Bayanaul itself is also covered by this car.
  3. R-174, starting at the suburbs of Semey and driving west up to Chagan.

You can distinguish these roads by the surrounding landscape and weather:

  1. The terrain is fairly flat, and the weather is cloudy. The car becomes blurred halfway between Botakara and Sartobe.
  2. The road is surrounded by small hills with exposed rocks, and the sun is high in the sky. While the car may appear blurred in Bayanaul, the coverage is easily recognizable thanks to the hilly terrain and the distinct late-autumn scenery.
  3. The landscape is extremely flat, and there isn’t a single cloud in the sky.

Note: Sometimes the antenna is not visible.

metas.name: Car with 6 Dots – Urban
metas.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with 6 Dots (image 1), you must be in Pavlodar.

Note: The same car also covers R-174, which in some spots near larger towns may resemble an urban area. However, you can distinguish it from Pavlodar by the fact that the dots are more faded (image 2).

metas.name: Car with a Black Dot and a White Dot
metas.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with a Black Dot and a White Dot (image 2):

  • M-38, starting at Pavlodar and driving southeast up to Semey.

Near Pavlodar, the white dot is less visible. The farther south you go, the lower the sun appears in the sky.

Note: The white dot appears on other roads as well, but not together with the black one.

metas.name: Car with a Bracket and a Bird Poop on the Bottom Right Metal Holder – Non-Urban
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with a Bracket and a Bird Poop on the Bottom Right Metal Holder (image 2):

  1. A17, starting east of the intersection above Abay and driving northeast up to Karaganda.
  2. A17, starting at the same location and driving south and then southwest up to Atasu.

You can distinguish these sections by driving direction, number of traffic lanes, and landscape:

  1. Driving northwest. The road has two lanes in one direction for the most of its length. It is frequently traveled by cars, and the closer you are to Karaganda, the heavier the traffic.
  2. Driving south or southwest. The road has only one lane per direction, except for a very short stretch near Abay. The car is often blurred, but you can still recognise this road by the surrounding landscape (image 3):
  • The weather is very sunny, with not a single cloud in the sky.
  • The terrain is slightly hilly, or you can see small hills in the distance. Sometimes the elevation changes are minimal, but it’s almost never completely flat.
  • The grass is dry and yellowish, with no large trees — only small bushes.

The same car with the poop on the metal holder also appears in Karaganda, its suburbs (including Saran), and Kokshetau, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account.
metas.footer:
Source: @Top 20 of Ukraine — big thanks for sharing the info!

Description and images - by @Docia. Some information has been updated or expanded.

metas.name: Car with a Bracket and a Dirty Back
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with a Bracket and a Dirty Back (image 2):

  1. A-27, starting in the suburbs of Aktobe, driving south through Kandyagash, then continuing via A-26 up to midway between Izembet and Dzhurun.
  2. A-27, starting in Kandyagash and driving southwest up to Zharly.

You can distinguish these roads by driving direction:

  1. Driving south. Additionally, many sections of the A-27 feature a parallel road under construction.
  2. Driving southwest.

Note: If you're driving southwest through an urban area, you're likely in Kandyagash.

metas.name: Car with a Bracket and a Dot on the Top Left – Non-Urban
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with a Bracket and a Dot on the Top Left (image 2):

  • A322, starting at Semey, driving northeast, then turning east on P-147 to Shemonaikha and then continuing via A3 (or an unlabeled road) to the intersection with A-9, before finally heading south to Oskemen.

You can distinguish these sections by driving direction, cloud coverage, and sun position.

Near Semey, the weather is quite cloudy. Around Novaya Suhl'ba, the sky becomes almost completely clear. The closer you get to Oskemen, the lower the sun is in the sky.

Note: There is another road covered by the car with the dot on the top left, but it has a parallel road under construction, and the coverage was done in late autumn.

Bonus: If you see this car driving through a city and there are street lamps with three square light sources along the road (image 3), you're in Shemonaikha.

metas.name: Car with a Dirty Back – Urban
metas.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Dirty Back (image 1), you must be either in Oskemen or Ridder.

In Ridder it is always very cloudy and mountainous, while in Oskemen most of the coverage was done during sunny days and the hills are much smaller.

Note: There are several dirty cars, but the smudge patterns vary — be careful not to confuse them.

metas.name: Car with a Faded Dot – Urban
metas.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Faded Dot (image 1), you must be in the southeastern part of Aktau, southern part of Zhanaozen, or occasionally in the southern part of Kulsary.

In Kulsary, the car often has a dirty rear window, unlike in Aktau and Zhanaozen — but this is not a fully reliable meta.

Note 1: The dot may be hard to see under intense sunlight.

Note 2: The same car also covered the A-33 between Say-Otes and Beyneu, which occasionally passes close to urban areas, so take that into account.

metas.name: Car with a Smudge on the Window – Urban
metas.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with a Smudge on the Window (image 1), you must be either in Zhezqazghan or Karazhal.

Note 1: The dirt on the rear window is sometimes barely visible.

Note 2: The same car appears on P-34 and A-17 near Karazhal, but these roads do not pass through any cities.

metas.name: Car with a Wire, a Bracket, and a Slightly Dirty Roof at the Back
metas.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with a Wire, a Bracket, and a Slightly Dirty Roof at the Back (image 2):

  • The unlabeled road, starting in the suburbs of Petropavl and driving east to the Russian border.

Note: You can confirm this road by the presence of a black box placed in the truck bed, touching the right side panel (image 3).
metas.footer:
Source: @Top 20 of Ukraine — big thanks for sharing the info!

Description and images - by @Docia.

metas.name: Car with Labeled Metal Holders – Non-Urban
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with Labeled Metal Holders (image 2):

  1. Unlabeled road north of Konaev, starting at the intersection with A3 (Avtomobil'nyy Most), driving north to the intersection near Kirbulak Grocery, turning onto the unpaved off-road, and continuing east to Ile River, and then driving north along the river into the middle of nowhere.
  2. A3, starting at the intersection west of Saryozek, driving north, up to the latitude of Tauracy (a small town located east of A3).

You can distinguish these roads by their driving direction and number of roadways:

  1. A single paved road, driving north. After turning onto the unpaved off-road, you first pass through flat grasslands (top part of image 3), and as you approach the Ile River, the terrain becomes hilly (bottom part of image 3). The car becomes blurred at the end of this section, but the distinct landscape should help you recognize it.
  2. A divided highway.
metas.footer:
Source: @Top 20 of Ukraine — big thanks for sharing the info!

Description and images - by @Docia. Some information has been updated or expanded.

metas.name: Car with Numerous Grey Dots – Non-Urban
metas.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with Numerous Grey Dots (image 2):

  • Unlabeled road, starting at Lesbek Batyr and driving south to the Uzbekistan border.

The coverage was captured during sunny weather with a completely clear sky. The landscape is barren, with only sparse grass.

Note: The same car also covered some roads in Zhetisay and Turkistan, which might sometimes appear as non-urban areas, so take that into account.
metas.footer:
Source: A Learnable Kazakhstan - by @Capi.

Description and images - by @Docia.

metas.name: Car with Numerous Grey Dots – Urban
metas.note:
If you are in an urban area and you see this Car with Numerous Grey Dots (image 1), you must be in the eastern part of Zhetisay (more likely) or in Turkistan (less likely).

You can distinguish these two cities by the appearance of the dirt on the bottom-left metal holder (image 2).

Note: This car also covered the unlabeled road between Lesbek Batyr and the Uzbekistan border, so take that into account.

metas.name: Car with Several Dots on the Left
metas.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Car with Several Dots on the Left (image 2):

  • A-27, starting at Dossor and driving southwest up to Atyrau.

The road drives among the desert and the weather is very sunny.

metas.name: Car with some Orange Dirt in the Bottom Left
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Car with some Orange Dirt in the Bottom Left (image 2):

  1. A33, starting just south of an unlabeled village and driving west into the center of Aktau.
  2. E-121, starting from a random offroad section near the intersection with R-114, driving north, then entering a divided highway and continuing a few kilometers west.

You can distinguish these two sections by the surrounding environment and the position of the sun:

  1. In this section, you can see buildings to the west or north. This coverage was done during the sunset.
  2. This road is surrounded by empty deserts and the sun is high.

Note: On the A33, near Aktau, the Partly Blurred 3-Part Car also appears.
metas.footer:
Source: A Learnable Kazakhstan - by @Capi.

Description and images - by @Docia. Some information has been updated or expanded.

metas.name: Clean Car with 4 Stripes and a Barely Visible Dot on the Right
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Clean Car with 4 Stripes and a Barely Visible Dot on the Right (image 2):

  1. P4, starting at Astana, driving northeast, then east up to Ekibastuz.
  2. An unlabeled road, driving southeast from Ekibastuz, then entering P27 and continuing south up to Korneevka.
  3. A short stretch of P27 south of Kalkaman.

You can distinguish these roads by number of roadways and driving direction:

  1. Divided highway.
  2. Single roadway. Never driving north or east. Near Bayanau the car is blurred, but you should be able to recognise this road, due to hilly terrain and sunny weather.
  3. Single roadway as well, but the car is driving northeast, north, or east.

Note: The dot on the right is sometimes hard to spot.
metas.footer:
Source: A Learnable Kazakhstan - by @Capi.

Description and images - by @Docia. Some information has been updated or expanded.

metas.name: Clean Car with a Bracket on the Divided Highway in Winter
metas.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Clean Car with a Bracket (image 2):

  • Divided highway between Saryozek and Taldykorgan (both directions).

This road is unique because, unlike other divided highways that were covered during winter, the car is almost perfectly clean.

Note 1: A small stretch of the road driving north from Taldykorgan is covered by a different car.

Note 2: The same clean car can appear on other divided highways near larger cities, so use this clue with caution.

metas.name: Clean Car with a Small Dot
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Clean Car with a Small Dot (image 2):

  • A3, starting at Taldykorgan, driving northeast to the intersection with P-130, then changing direction and driving southeast up to Druzhba.

This car is unique, because it is very clean, unlike others used during winter on major roads.

You can distinguish different sections of this route based on driving direction and some other clues:

  • From Taldykorgan to the intersection east of Qyzylagash, there's a second roadway under construction.
  • Between the intersection and the area around Inbek, an off-road track runs parallel to the main road on the north side (except when driving south of Zhansügirov).
  • On the P-130 segment, you're driving alongside large mountains clearly visible to the south.

Note: The car is blurred arround the intersection with A-354.

metas.name: Dirty Car on the Divided Highway
metas.note:
The following divided highway (image 1) is covered by this Dirty Car (image 2):

– A1, starting in the suburbs of Kokshetau and driving southeast around Shchuchinsk up to the intersection with R-228.

Note: The same dirty car also covers the A1 between Shchuchinsk and Astana, but that stretch features three lanes in one direction, unlike the section north of Shchuchinsk.

metas.name: Dirty Car with 1 Dot on the Right
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Dirty Car with 1 Dot on the Right (image 2):

  • A3, starting from the intersection above Konaev (Avtomobil'nyy Most), driving northeast, passing around Saryozek and continuing via A353 east to the intersection near Kakinino, then turning south and ending near Нұрым, close to Altyn Emel National Park.

The A3 up to Saryozek is a divided highway covered in both directions. The remaining sections are single roadways.

Bonus: If you see this car driving through the city and there are poles painted yellow and red (image 3), you must be in Saryozek.
metas.footer:
Source: A Learnable Kazakhstan - by @Capi.

Description and images - by @Docia.

metas.name: Dirty Car with a Lot of Dots
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Dirty Car with a Lot of Dots (image 2):

  1. R-217, starting at Atbasar suburbs, driving southeast to the intersection with R-260, and continuing up to the intersection with A-16.
  2. R-217 off-road, starting at the intersection east of Kiyma, driving south and then west to Trudovoye.

The weather on these roads is generally cloudy. The sun is visible only near the suburbs of Atbasar and on the off-road section of R-217.

You can distinguish these sections by the presence of pavement and the landscape:

  1. R-217 main road and R-260 are both paved:
    • R-217 is very flat.
    • R-260 is more hilly, and in the final few kilometers, the pavement quality becomes very poor and eventually disappears entirely.
  2. R-217 off-road is unpaved, but remains very flat, unlike the more uneven terrain of R-260.

Note 1: If you're in a semi-urban area and see this car, you're most likely in the suburbs of Derzhavinsk.

Note 2: A similar dirty car covers R-214 between Kokshetau and Atbasar, but that car has a bracket — unlike the one used on the roads south of Atbasar.
metas.footer:
Source: A Learnable Kazakhstan - by @Capi.

Description and images - by @Docia. Some information has been updated or expanded.

metas.name: Ereymentau Car with 1 Dot on the Right – Urban
metas.note:
If you are in an urban area and see this Car with 1 Dot on the Right (image 1), you must be in Ereymentau or its suburbs.

Note: It is hard to spot this dot, but it is very useful as it only appears in this village.

metas.name: Forest Fire Coverage
metas.note:
In the southern part of Oskemen (image 1) the coverage was done during a forest fire at sunset, giving the sky an orange/pink hue and making it very cloudy (image 2).

You can occasionally see black smoke.

metas.name: Fort-Shevchenko Pole-Mounted Street Signs
metas.note: Street signs in Fort-Shevchenko have white text on a blue background, enclosed in a black metal frame with a pointed end (image 1).
metas.footer:
Source: Street signs of Kazakhstan - by @kotyu.

Description and images - by @Docia.

metas.name: Kokshetau Buses
metas.note:
There are two types of buses commonly seen in Kokshetau. Both share the same color scheme: they are white with orange mirrors and an orange lower part (image 1).

On the sides, one model has the white 'INVIVO' text on a red background, while the other features "OLYMP" written on a white background, along with an orange roof.

Note: Similar buses can occasionally be spotted in Shymkent, but they feature the Shymkent city logo on the side (image 2).

metas.name: Koschi Vibes – Urban
metas.note:
The coverage in Koschi, a small city in Akmola south of Astana, was taken in November during a period of heavy overcast. The vegetation appears lifeless, while the soil has a distinct orange hue.

The area is undergoing extensive development, with many roads freshly paved and the sidewalks either newly laid or still under construction. Dark gravel is scattered throughout, and the asphalt is intensely black. Most of the buildings in the city are made from yellow and orange brick.

The overall scenery is shown in image 1.

metas.name: Kostanay Bus Stops
metas.note: In Kostanay, you can occasionally spot these simple brown bus stops featuring the city's logo on the glass (image 1).

metas.name: Kulsary Street Lamps
metas.note:
In Kulsary, you can find these street lamps with exceptionally tall photocell mounted on top (image 1).

Note: Photocells are also present in other cities, but they are usually much smaller and barely noticeable.

metas.name: May Coverage
metas.note:
Alataou (image 1), a small settlement 25 km east of Almaty, is the only place in Kazakhstan that was covered in May. Snow-capped mountains are visible to the south, the weather is very sunny, and the vegetation is lush green (image 2) — unlike in the surrounding areas, which were covered in winter.

Note: You can confirm this clue by checking for the presence of the wire in the car trunk (image 3).

metas.name: Nearly Clean Car with a Wire and a Bracket in the Desert
metas.note:
The following roads (image 1) are covered by this Nearly Clean Car with a Wire and a Bracket (image 2):

  1. An unlabeled road starting from Aktau, driving northwest, bypassing Aqshuqyr, passing through Aktau Airport, and continuing up to Fort-Schevchenko.
  2. An unlabeled road starting from Zhanaozen and driving south to the Turkmenistan border.
  3. An unlabeled road starting from Zhanaozen and driving generally in the northeast direction to Beket-Ata.

The car on these roads might be slightly dirty, but it lacks the characteristic dots, smudges, or other marks. The surrounding landscape is desert, and the weather is sunny, with the sun high in the sky.

You can distinguish these three sections by driving direction.

Note 1: Cars with a wire and a bracket on other roads may also appear nearly clean because dirt patterns are hard to see under intense sunlight.

Note 2: A similar car can also appear on various other roads near major cities, so use this clue with caution.

metas.name: Pedestrian Signs Attached Sideways
metas.note:
The vast majority of pedestrian signs in Karaganda and nearby cities are mounted sideways (image 1) to traffic light poles, rather than on separate vertical rods (it applies only to pedestrian crossings controlled by traffic lights). These signs usually lack the yellow reflective border commonly seen elsewhere.

Be careful — sideways-mounted pedestrian signs can be found in other cities as well, just less frequently. However, if you see multiple signs without yellow outlines mounted this way, you're likely in the Karaganda region.

Bonus tip: In Astana, pedestrian signs are never used at crossings controlled by traffic lights. It can help in 50:50 cases between Karaganda and Astana.

Source: Street signs of Kazakhstan - by @kotyu.

metas.name: Petropavl Bus Stops
metas.note:
In Petropavl, you can commonly see brown bus stops with a roof angled slightly upwards and a bench mounted asymmetrically on the right side (image 1).

Note: Similar bus stops can be found in Stepnogorsk, but there the bench is mounted symmetrically, unlike in Petropavl.

metas.name: Petropavl Pole-Mounted Street Signs
metas.note: Pole-mounted street signs in Petropavl have white text in both Kazakh and Russian, divided by an arrow, on a green background, enclosed in a white metal frame with a pointed end (image 1).

metas.name: Road Through Rolling Hills and Grassy Fields
metas.note: There is no meta for the road between Shymkent and Zhetisay (image 1), but it has a unique vibe. The car drives south through rolling, grassy hills (image 2). It's very sunny, without a single cloud in the sky. The A-2 section is a divided highway. After leaving the A-2, the road becomes a single roadway.

metas.name: Shchuchinsk Pole Paint
metas.note:
In Shchuchinsk, poles are rarely painted yellow with a short red stripe at the top (image 1).

Be careful — similar pole markings can also be found in Atbasar, Derzhavinsk, Kandyagash, and Tobyl. Here are some tips to help tell them apart:

  • In Atbasar, the yellow paint appears more like a cream color, as if yellow and white were mixed.
  • In Derzhavinsk, the coverage was done during overcast weather by the dirty car with a lot of dots (top part of image 2).
  • In Kandyagash, the coverage was done by the car with a bracket and dirty back (medium part of image 2).
  • In Tobyl, the coverage was done by the car with 4 stripes and a white sticker (bottom part of image 2).

metas.name: Shymkent Bus
metas.note:
In Shymkent, you can commonly spot these eco-friendly, gas-powered Yutong buses painted in a light green and white color scheme (image 1).

These buses are also used in other cities across Kazakhstan, but if you can see the side of the bus, you can distinguish it by the presence of the red Shymkent logo. Its color stands out against the background, even from a distance.

Note: Sometimes the bus may be dirty, making the logo less visible.

metas.name: Stepnogorsk Bus Stops
metas.note:
In Stepnogorsk, you can commonly see these brown bus stops with a roof angled slightly upwards and a bench mounted on the bottom of the horizontal bar (image 1). They typically feature two brown trash bins, one on each side of the bus stop.

Note: Similar bus stops can be found in Petropavl, but there the bench is mounted asymmetrically, unlike in Stepnogorsk.

metas.name: Taldykorgan Pole-Mounted Street Signs
metas.note:
Street signs in Taldykorgan have black text on a white background, enclosed in a white metal frame rounded on both sides (image 1). They are attached on their backs to traffic light poles.

Be careful — similar signs can be found in Kokshetau, but they are side-attached to a metal pole designed exclusively for them, and the frame is rounded only on one side (image 2).

metas.name: Trams
metas.note:
Trams (image 1) can be found in Pavlodar, Oskemen, and Temirtau.

You can distinguish these cities by tram appearance, line orientation and car meta:

  • Trams in Pavlodar are more modern than those in Oskemen and Temirtau. They often feature a red-and-white design. Sometimes they use other colors, but they are usually covered with advertisements and generally look clean and well-maintained.

  • Trams in Temirtau and Oskemen have older designs and look quite similar. They typically have a blue (sometimes red) and white color scheme, and may also be covered in graffiti. You can tell these two cities apart using other clues:

    All of Temirtau was covered by a clean car. In Oskemen, several car types were used, but the sections near the tram lines were covered either by a dirty car or by a car with a bracket.

    You can also use the street orientation as a clue — I’ve marked all tram lines in both cities on the map (image 2).

Note 1: You can also find the remnants of tram infrastructure in Almaty, so if you see only tram tracks, consider that city as well.

Note 2: Be careful not to confuse tram tracks with train tracks, which are visible in various cities.

metas.name: Uralsk Street Lamps
metas.note: In Uralsk, you can find these street lamps with three separate lights arranged in an ascending pattern (image 1).

metas.name: Very Dirty Car with a Bracket
metas.note:
The following road (image 1) is covered by this Very Dirty Car with a Bracket (image 2):

  • R-214, starting at Kokshetau and driving south to Atbasar.

From Kokshetau to Zerenda, the car has noticeable 'vertical smudges' on the roof (top part of image 2). Around Zerenda, it begins to rain and the road becomes wet — the smudges get washed off, but the car remains very dirty (bottom part of image 2). As you approach Atbasar, the sun begins to set. The coverage on this road was done in autumn during overcast weather.

Note: A similar dirty car covers R-217 and R-260 south of Atbasar, but that one lacks a bracket — unlike the car used on R-214.

metas.name: Zhetisay Surface-Mounted Street Signs
metas.note:
In Zhetisay, you can commonly find blue street signs attached to fences or buildings. They feature a white inner line that doesn’t touch the edges of the sign, with a QR code on the right side (image 1).

While the design may seem fairly generic, these details make the signs stand out.

metas.name: Zhezqazghan Scraped Roads
metas.note:
Many roads in Zhezqazghan are in poor condition and are undergoing maintenance. The top layer of asphalt is often scraped off, revealing shallow ruts on the layer beneath (image 1). Pieces of old asphalt are frequently scattered around, and construction machinery is commonly seen throughout the city.

Zhezqazghan is built on a small hill in a rather desert-like region, so the terrain is often inclined, and the vegetation tends to look dry.

Note: This meta isn’t very reliable, but if no stronger clues are available, it can still help.
